rationale: Fatigue became less common in a post-COVID comparison that used the same ungraded oral peanut oil in both arms. A rat dopamine formulation also used peanut oil as a carrier and recorded no fatigue outcome. Fatigue severity after cold-pressed peanut oil in Parkinson disease remains unresolved.

Both post-COVID groups received the same ungraded oral peanut oil and reported joint pain. Animal and topical comparisons use other routes. A dopamine nanoparticle experiment used peanut oil as a carrier and did not measure pain. Refined peanut oil and clinical Parkinson pain remain unresolved.

Sunflower comparator trials report mixed attention, memory and executive outcomes. A Mediterranean diet intervention replaced several oils including sunflower, giving a favorable global cognitive result but an inconclusive verbal-fluency comparison. No reviewed comparison isolates cold-pressed sunflower oil and Parkinson executive function.

Clinical extracts and powders give mixed anxiety results, and the Parkinson extract study has no posted results. A topical fresh-ginger mixture gave favorable IBS quality-of-life observations. Oral extract experiments report favorable rodent anxiety-like measures. Preparation, population and endpoint do not resolve grated ginger and clinical Parkinson anxiety.

The cooked barley-flour study reports anxiety improvement in both periods and an inconclusive barley–rice contrast. Roasted barley comparisons gave mixed within-condition results. Pearl barley was a shared vehicle in a mouse locomotion experiment. Evidence for boiled intact barley and Parkinson anxiety remains unresolved.
